title.en: An Act to Amend Sections Fourteen Hundred and Eighty-Five, Fourteen Hundred and Ninety-One, and Fourteen Hundred and Ninety-Two of the Administrative Code for the Purpose of Permitting the Transfer of Cigars Under Bond, and for Other

text.en:
Section fourteen hundred and eighty-five of the Administrative Code is hereby amended to read
"Section 1485. Removal of spirits or cigars under bond.- Spirits requiring rectification may be removed from
the01 place of their manufacture to some other establishment for the purpose of rectification without the
prepayment of the specific tax provided the distiller removing such spirits and the rectifier receiving them
shall file with the Collector of Internal Revenue their joint bond conditioned for the future payment by the
rectifier of the specific tax that may be due on any finished product, and cigars may be removed by a
manufacturer of tobacco products owning and operating a branch factory separate from his principal factory,
from the branch factory to the principal factory, for exportation, without the prepayment of the specific tax
provided the manufacturer shall file with the Collector of Internal Revenue his bond conditioned for the future
payment of the specific tax that may be due on the finished product."

Section fourteen hundred and ninety-one of the same Code is hereby amended to read as follows:
"Section 1491. Removal of tobacco products without prepayment of tax.-Products of tobacco entirely unfit for
chewing or smoking may be removed free of tax for agricultural or industrial use, under such conditions as
may be prescribed in the regulations of the Bureau ; and stemmed leaf tobacco, fine-cut shorts, the refuse of
fine-cut chewing tobacco, refuse, scraps, cuttings, clippings, and sweepings of tobacco may be sold in bulk as
raw material by one manufacturer directly to another, under such conditions as may be prescribed in the
regulations of the Bureau, without the prepayment of the tax.
" 'Stemmed leaf tobacco,' as herein used, means leaf tobacco which has had the stem or midrib removed. The
term does not include broken leaf tobacco."

Section fourteen hundred and ninety-two of the same Code is hereby amended to read as
"Section 1492. Specific tax on cigars and cigarettes.-On cigars and cigarettes (except handmade cigars and
cigarettes prepared by the consumer for his own consumption and so used) there shall be collected the
following taxes:
"1. When the manufacturer's usual wholesale value, less the amount of the tax, is twenty-five pesos per
thousand, or less, on each thousand, two pesos.
"2. When the manufacturer's usual wholesale value, less the amount of the tax, is more than twenty-five but
not more than fifty pesos per thousand, on each thousand, four pesos.

"3. When the manufacturer's usual wholesale value, less the amount of the tax, exceeds fifty pesos per
thousand, on each thousand, six pesos.
"(b) Cigarettes-
"1. Weighing not more than two kilograms per thousand, on each thousand, one peso and twenty centavos.
"2. Weighing more than two kilograms per thousand, on each thousand, two pesos."
Approved, February 15, 1918.
